How a block of glass learned to hold light

Glass has held light in three ways. Turn each one and see what is left.

  1. A window lets light through.

    For 3,500 years glass has done one thing with light: let it pass. Whatever you see in a window is somewhere else, and nothing stays when you look away.

  2. A plate keeps a picture.

    A photograph, a screen and even a hologram on film hold their image on a surface. Turn one 90° and the picture becomes a line. It was only ever drawn for one side.

  3. A block holds the light itself.

    Inside the Cube, two infrared beams cross. Where they meet, and only there, the glass glows. Voxmere moves that meeting point through the whole block 30 times a second, so every point of the image sits at its own depth. Turn it to 180° and you are looking at the mountain’s far side.

Turn it yourself.

Drag or swipe the Cube, or use the arrow keys. Every side you find was always there.

What it holds
Glass
  • Peak: an alpine survey in 13 contour lines. The north face is the steep one.
  • Ammonite: a spiral shell of 3.4 turns. Face-on it is a spiral, edge-on a lens.
  • Orrery: four planets on tilted orbits, moving. The Cube redraws its whole volume 30 times a second.

Two sizes.

The same glass and the same light. Cube 20 holds eight times the image volume, and weighs seven times as much.

Before you reserve

Is the deposit really refundable?

Yes. Until your Cube ships you can cancel from your confirmation email or from this page on the same device, and the CHF 100 comes back to your card in full.

When is the rest charged?

The balance, the price minus your deposit, is charged on the day your Cube ships, never before. We write first to confirm the date and your delivery address.

Can I change size or glass later?

Yes, any time before shipping. Moving from Cube 10 to Cube 20 keeps your place in the batch; the balance changes with the price.

What do I need to use it?

A power socket and Wi-Fi. Images come from the Voxmere app for iOS, Android and macOS, which opens glTF and USDZ files and ships with a library of live scenes.
